correctness.rationale: The nonnegative reduced next-generation matrix is diagonally similar to an affine symmetric rank-one-plus-diagonal matrix. Its fixed Rayleigh trial quotient equals one, with strictness for all unequal sizes at nonzero mixing parameter. Convexity gives monotonicity, and simple eigenvalue perturbation gives the exact quadratic coefficient. Two-dimensional Krylov compression yields the sharp three-moment envelope; equality is proved by invariant share-value classes and a quadratic-polynomial obstruction for three distinct sizes. The exact rational two-community witness crosses the epidemic invasion threshold. The bundled checker passed 4,400 spectral and 3,216 envelope cases plus exact symbolic checks; finite tests are not treated as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The source supplies the two-group invasion matrix and the planted-partition normalization, but not a uniform result over all finite numbers of groups or the global three-moment bound with its exact equality class. The 2023 general positive-preference results fix each group activity, a different admissible contact family. Nearby published contact-allocation and commuter results optimize different objects and constraints. Priority is literature-bounded, not an assertion that no unindexed stronger result exists.
residual_risks: An unindexed general spectral bound for affine diagonal-plus-rank-one matrices might already give an equivalent sharp Ritz expression and equality class.
The 2026 paper discusses two-group community imbalance; the illustrative two-sided threshold alone is a corollary of existing two-group formulas and is not asserted to be independently new.
An independent mathematical and bibliographic priority review has not been performed.

value.rationale: The new sharp low-order moment envelope captures an arbitrary finite number of imbalanced communities and identifies exactly when those aggregate moments determine the full invasion reproduction number. The model holds total mean contact degree and biological susceptibility-transmissibility products fixed, so the strict random-mixing optimum and two-sided threshold crossing isolate a structural effect of unequal group sizes; neither finding can be attributed to unequal biological risk or increased total contacts. The source gives only two-community formulas and descriptive observations; this result provides an interpretable all-size quantitative bound and exact equality classification. Predictive relevance is limited to the specified mean-field invasion criterion.
